body.statement: For \(\ell=3\), \(r_{\beta}(3)=4\): on a Zariski-dense relatively Euclidean-open subset of \(\mathcal O_{3,3}\), the augmented Jacobian \(D(\Phi_{3,3},\beta)\) has rank strictly larger than \(D\Phi_{3,3}\) along preimages in \(\Theta_{3,3}\) and \(\beta\) varies within every legal fiber. At order four, \(\mathfrak A^{\mathrm{id}}_{3,4}\ne\varnothing\), and the union of its domains \(\mathcal U_{\chi}\cap\mathcal O_{3,4}\) contains a nonempty relatively Zariski-open subset; on this union every covering chart returns the common legal-fiber effect, and outside all chart domains every recovery map returns \(\bot\). Consequently, the Tramontano--Kivva--Salehkaleybar--Kiyavash--Drton workflow specialized to three latent confounders can replace its sufficient input \(C_{\le k(3)}=C_{\le7}\) by \(C_{\le4}\) on that regular legal image, while no procedure using only \(C_{\le3}\) can report a generically identified point effect on the stated open lower-fiber locus.
body.justification: The exact three-latent case converts a fiber calculation into a seven-to-four reduction in required empirical cumulant order and a sharp order-three nonidentification decision.
body.gap: Tramontano et al., Theorems 3.4--3.5, specialize to the sufficient order \(k(3)=7\) and do not show either order-four sufficiency from the complete tensor or generic failure at order three.
body.consumer: For \(\ell=3\), CEId-from-Moments can stop after estimating \(C_{\le4}\) instead of \(C_{\le7}\); if only \(C_{\le3}\) is available on the open lower-fiber locus, it must return nonidentification rather than a selected point estimate.
